description: Productivity page — top-level tab housing three sub-views (Plans & Tasks / Coordinator / Knowledge) backed by the productivity-stack PG tables (plans, tasks, reviews, productivity_knowledge, coordinator_decisions, snapshots). The plan/task board is a three-column read-only board: a plans list with a 'Show archived' toggle (left, 25%), a tasks-for-selected-plan list grouped by phase with a collapsible Reflection panel above it (middle, 50%), and a task-detail panel showing claims, deps, latest review summary, and worker session metadata (right, 25%). The Coordinator dashboard stacks five panels — PlanRecommendations card, the medium-confidence Recommendations queue, an LLM-driven Advisories list (advise-with-text rows from the last hour), an Escalations list of destructive auto_acted=false rows (kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree, escalate, escalate-with-text), and a chronological Decision log of the last 200 coordinator_decisions filterable by rule (A-E or LLM) and action. Below the spec-locked five-panel block two observability panels are appended: a File Activity panel (live file-registry holders + hot files/sessions) and a Fleet Health panel (Row 9 Phase 4 — per-machine liveness state from coord.machines, in-flight agent counts, and the active coord.alerts list with severity rollup, polled ~1 Hz from coord's /coord/fleet/health + /coord/alerts). The Knowledge browser is rendered both inline (Knowledge sub-view) and as a modal globally triggered by Ctrl+Shift+K; both modes share the same FTS-only search surface with an area-filter dropdown and click-to-expand result rows. A top-bar selector switches between the three sub-views and is also driven by the `productivity-set-view` window CustomEvent (used by useAppNavigation alias routing and by the Recommendations / Reflection / PlanRecommendations cross-component triggers). The page is a window into orchestration logic: tasks transition pending → ready → assigned → running → review → (done | needs_fix | escalated), reviews flow through a confidence-gated handler (auto-merge ≥ 0.85, user-approval queue [0.7, 0.85), coordinator action below), and the Coordinator's auto-act boundary keeps destructive actions advisory-only.

groups.description: Per productivity-stack §2 (data model) and §5 (Coordinator state machine), every task lives in exactly one of nine states: pending → ready (when all dependsOn are done) → assigned → running → review → (done | needs_fix | escalated) — with cancelled as a terminal abort. needs_fix retries cap at 3 before forced escalation. Reviews are confidence-gated: verdict=approved AND confidence ≥ 0.85 → auto-merge (no UI surface); confidence in [0.7, 0.85) → user-approval Recommendations queue; confidence < 0.7 OR verdict in {needs_fix, escalate} → coordinator action. The board is the only surface where these state transitions are user-visible — incorrect states or transitions on display indicate a bug in the underlying tasks/reviews tables or in their derivation.
groups.name: Domain Logic — Task State Machine & Confidence Gates

groups.description: The server-enforced auto-act boundary (productivity-stack §5) guarantees that destructive or LLM-judgement actions ALWAYS persist with auto_acted=false regardless of whether the agent claimed to act: kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree, cancel-task, escalate, escalate-with-text, advise-with-text, idle-no-action. These are surfaced as advisory chips in the Decision log and route to the Escalations panel (destructive subset) or the Advisories panel (advise-with-text only). Every Decision log row also displays an 'auto' (emerald) or 'advisory' (amber) chip based on autoActed — a kill-session or force-promote-to-worktree row showing 'auto' indicates the server boundary was bypassed and is a critical safety bug.

groups.description: The Decision log panel queries getCoordinatorDecisions(limit=200, {rule, action}) and renders rows sorted by createdAt descending. Three independent filters are offered. (1) Rule-filter select (data-ui-bridge-id `productivity.coord-decision-log-rule-filter`): options `all` (value=''), A, B, C, D, E, LLM, idle, plus `deconflict` (set by rows emitted by the Rust deconflicter loop in coordinator/deconflicter.rs). (2) Action-filter select (data-ui-bridge-id `productivity.coord-decision-log-action-filter`): options `all` plus the 11 CoordinatorActionName values: assign-task, pause-session, merge-task, reassign-needs-fix, escalate, advise-with-text, escalate-with-text, kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree, cancel-task, idle-no-action. (3) Source-filter chip group (data-ui-bridge-id `productivity.decision-source-filter`): three button chips with `data-source-filter-key` of `all`, `ai`, `deconflicter`. `all` (default-pressed) returns every row. `ai` keeps rows whose `sessionId` does NOT start with the literal `deconflicter-` prefix (i.e., the AI Coordinator PTY skill's rule-A-through-E and LLM fires). `deconflicter` keeps rows whose `sessionId` starts with `deconflicter-` (currently only the Rust loop's reserved `deconflicter-rust`). The source filter is purely client-side over the existing `getCoordinatorDecisions` payload — no extra HTTP call — and is independent of the rule/action selects (intersected with them). Active chip carries `aria-pressed="true"`; chips are styled with the existing bg-muted/border-border palette. Changing any of the three filters re-renders rows. Each row shows action (color-keyed by autoActed), rule, iteration, time, optional targetId, and full reasoning.
groups.name: Decision Log — Filters & Row Cap

groups.description: The Coordinator sub-tab renders a single-line lease-status pill (data-ui-bridge-id `productivity.lease-status-pill`) reflecting the `coord.coordinator_leader` row state for the AI Coordinator PTY skill (the user-driven, expensive coordinator). Three derived states render different text + `data-lease-status` attribute values: (a) `active` — pill renders "AI Coordinator: running (<short-instance-id>, <relative-age>)" with `data-lease-status="active"` and emerald styling, lease row exists and `leased_until > NOW()`; (b) `stale` — pill renders "AI Coordinator: stale lease (last heartbeat <age> ago)" with `data-lease-status="stale"` and amber styling, lease row exists but `leased_until <= NOW()` (renewal timer skipped or the PTY died without releasing); (c) vacant — pill renders "AI Coordinator: vacant" with `data-lease-status="vacant"` and neutral styling, no lease row found. The label uses "AI Coordinator" (not bare "Coordinator") to distinguish from the Rust deconflicter loop which writes its own decisions and has no lease pill (intentional per §5.3 — the deconflicter is invisible at the lease-pill surface; its activity is visible only through the Source filter chip in the decision-log panel, see `productivity-decision-log-filters`). The pill is read-only — the Launch / Stop coordinator buttons live in a sibling header row (`productivity.launch-coordinator`, `productivity.stop-coordinator`, `productivity.launch-coordinator-claude-skill`). Renderer: CoordinatorLeaseStatusPill function in CoordinatorDashboard.tsx; data source is the `currentLeader()` query joined with a NOW() comparison in the dashboard's loadLeaderState path.
groups.name: Coordinator Lease Status Pill

groups.description: Each Recommendations queue card (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-recommendation-card with data-review-id) exposes three actions: Approve (emerald), Reject (red), and Open task (muted external-link button). Approve calls approveRecommendation(reviewId) which marks the underlying review as approved and flips the task to 'done'; on success both the recommendation list and the decision log are refreshed. Reject calls rejectRecommendation(reviewId) and refreshes the recommendation list only. Open task dispatches both 'productivity-set-view' (plans) AND 'productivity-select-task' so the user lands on the plan/task board with that task pre-selected. While a row's action is in flight, all three buttons are disabled. ReviewBadge in the terminal also dispatches 'productivity-select-recommendation' which highlights a card here in amber and scrolls it into view.
groups.name: Recommendations Queue — Approve / Reject / Open Task

groups.description: Each panel handles three lifecycle states. LOADING: a small spinner (Loader2 animate-spin) + grey muted text (e.g. 'Loading plans…', 'Loading tasks…', 'Loading detail…', 'Computing recommendations…', 'Loading reflection…'). ERROR: a soft empty state with explanatory italic muted copy — never a crashed page (try/catch wrappers in fetchPlans / loadDecisions / etc. coerce errors into empty results so an unmigrated backend renders cleanly). EMPTY: instructional muted copy that explains how to populate the surface (e.g. 'Run /decompose-plan', 'Run /summarize-session', 'Once /coordinate is running'). The PlansList specifically renders 'Plan registry unavailable. The backend command may not be registered yet.' on error.

groups.description: The PlanRecommendations card at the top of the Coordinator dashboard renders up to 3 candidate plans (server-ranked by getPlanRecommendations — cheap-rule only, no LLM). Each card row shows a ListChecks icon + plan title (or planId fallback), reasoning text (e.g. '3 ready tasks, 2 idle sessions, no upcoming-claim conflicts'), and an 'Open plan' button (ArrowRight icon) that dispatches productivity-set-view (plans) and productivity-select-plan (planId) so the plan/task board lands on the candidate. The empty state explicitly directs the user to /decompose-plan on a vetted plan. The card header shows 'top {N}' where N is rows.length.
groups.name: Plan Recommendations Card — Top-K Candidates

states.description: The page renders a top bar with a 'Productivity' heading, three sub-view tabs (Plans & Tasks, Coordinator, Knowledge) with lucide-react icons (ClipboardList, Bot, BookOpen), and a right-aligned 'Knowledge' button that opens the modal browser. Below the top bar the active sub-view is rendered into a flex-1 content area. The active sub-view defaults to 'plans' and can be switched by clicking a tab or by dispatching a `productivity-set-view` CustomEvent.
states.name: Productivity Shell

states.description: The page uses a typography hierarchy that follows the runner's design tokens: the page-title 'Productivity' uses the `text-h2` heading class, sub-view tab labels use text-sm font-medium, panel headers use text-sm font-semibold, list-row primary text uses text-sm, and metadata/timestamps use text-xs or [11px]/[10px] muted variants. Text-visibility (foreground vs background) is also covered here because every text element must be legible against its panel background.
states.name: Visual Design — Typography

states.description: The page uses the runner's neutral panel/background tokens (`bg-background`, `bg-card/30`, `bg-card/40`) for surfaces, `border-border` for separators, and a small palette of semantic accent colors keyed to status: blue (ready/running), cyan (assigned), purple (review/reflection/advisory), amber (needs_fix/escalation/advisory-only), emerald (done/auto-acted/approve), red (escalated/decline). These accents appear on borders, badge backgrounds, and badge text.
states.name: Visual Design — Color Scheme

states.description: The plan/task board uses a fixed 25% / 50% / 25% three-column flex layout with explicit minWidth on the side columns (220px plans, 260px detail). The Coordinator dashboard centers its panel stack at max-w-5xl with gap-4 between panels and p-4 internal padding. Rows in lists use border-b border-border/60 dividers with px-3 py-2 padding. Every interactive button has at least p-1 to guarantee a comfortable hit target.
states.name: Visual Design — Spacing & Layout

states.description: The Plans & Tasks sub-view renders three columns. LEFT (25%): PlansList with header ('Plans' h2 + Show-archived checkbox + refresh button) and a scrollable plan-row list. Each plan row shows the plan title (or markdownPath basename fallback), a PlanStatus badge, an optional 2-line summary, and the markdownPath in monospace muted text. The active plan has bg-primary/10 + border-primary left rail. MIDDLE (50%): collapsible Reflection panel above + TasksList below. The TasksList groups by phaseName (UPPERCASE phase header bg-muted/20) with rows sorted by sequenceInPhase showing the sequence #, the first line of the description, and a TaskStatus badge. Each row has a chevron to expand the full description. RIGHT (25%): TaskDetailPanel showing Status (badge + 2-col dl grid: Phase, Sequence, Assigned, Started, Completed), Expected file claims (with conflict badge when other tasks claim the same path), Depends on, Latest review summary, Worker session, and Notes.
states.name: Plans & Tasks — Three-Column Structure

states.description: The Coordinator dashboard renders six vertically-stacked panels in a fixed order: (1) PlanRecommendations 'Coordinator suggests next plan' card; (2) RecommendationsPanel — medium-confidence approved review queue; (3) AdvisoriesPanel — LLM advise-with-text rows from the last hour; (4) DeferralsPanel — Rule B deferral advisories (held-lock + cross-task) grouped by targetId, each row carries a force-assign session-picker override fired via POST /coordinator/dispatch-action; (5) EscalationsPanel — open destructive recommendations the agent flagged advisory-only; (6) DecisionLogPanel — chronological feed of last 200 coordinator_decisions rows filterable by rule (A-E or LLM) and action. Each panel is wrapped in a border-border + bg-card/30 rounded-lg section with its own header (icon + title + count chip + Refresh button) and a content area that handles error / empty / populated states.
states.name: Coordinator Dashboard — Six-Panel Stack

states.description: The KnowledgeBrowser renders in two modes from the same component: 'modal' (overlay with backdrop + dialog role + Esc-to-close + close X button) and 'inline' (full-height panel with no backdrop or close button). Both modes share: a Search input (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-search-input, placeholder 'Search knowledge…', Enter triggers search), an area-filter dropdown (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-area-filter, populated dynamically from distinct areas in the current hit set with 'All areas' default), a Search submit button (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-search-submit, disabled when query is blank), a results list (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-results), and a footer showing the result count. Each result row is keyed by hit.row.id with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-result-row, shows area pill + session id + score + summary, and click toggles a body disclosure rendering hit.row.body in a monospace pre block.
states.name: Knowledge Browser — Modal & Inline Modes

states.description: Per productivity-stack §2 (data model) and §5 (Coordinator state machine), every task lives in exactly one of nine states: pending → ready (when all dependsOn are done) → assigned → running → review → (done | needs_fix | escalated) — with cancelled as a terminal abort. needs_fix retries cap at 3 before forced escalation. Reviews are confidence-gated: verdict=approved AND confidence ≥ 0.85 → auto-merge (no UI surface); confidence in [0.7, 0.85) → user-approval Recommendations queue; confidence < 0.7 OR verdict in {needs_fix, escalate} → coordinator action. The board is the only surface where these state transitions are user-visible — incorrect states or transitions on display indicate a bug in the underlying tasks/reviews tables or in their derivation.
states.name: Domain Logic — Task State Machine & Confidence Gates

states.description: The server-enforced auto-act boundary (productivity-stack §5) guarantees that destructive or LLM-judgement actions ALWAYS persist with auto_acted=false regardless of whether the agent claimed to act: kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree, cancel-task, escalate, escalate-with-text, advise-with-text, idle-no-action. These are surfaced as advisory chips in the Decision log and route to the Escalations panel (destructive subset) or the Advisories panel (advise-with-text only). Every Decision log row also displays an 'auto' (emerald) or 'advisory' (amber) chip based on autoActed — a kill-session or force-promote-to-worktree row showing 'auto' indicates the server boundary was bypassed and is a critical safety bug.
states.name: Domain Logic — Coordinator Auto-Act Boundary

states.description: The ReflectionPanel renders a per-plan rollup composed by the get_reflection backend command. The header shows plan title · status · short version-hash (first 8 chars). The 5-tile stat row shows totalTasks, completedTasks, escalatedTasks, avgConfidence, and knowledgeCount. Aggregate invariants per plan §2 + plan §5: avgConfidence is null when no reviews exist (rendered as '—', NOT '0%'); knowledgeCount equals the number of productivity_knowledge rows linked to this plan's tasks; totalTasks equals the count of TaskRow rows for this planId; completedTasks counts tasks with status 'Done'; escalatedTasks counts tasks with status 'Escalated'. Two list sections follow: 'Top knowledge' (top-5 entries with area pill + summary, click switches to Knowledge sub-view filtered by area) and 'Review trail' (every review row with verdict badge + confidence + relative time + open-session link).
states.name: Reflection Panel — Aggregate Correctness

states.description: The Decision log panel queries getCoordinatorDecisions(limit=200, {rule, action}) and renders rows sorted by createdAt descending. The rule-filter select (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-decision-log-rule-filter) offers options 'all' (value=''), A, B, C, D, E, LLM, idle. The action-filter select (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-decision-log-action-filter) offers options 'all' plus the 11 CoordinatorActionName values: assign-task, pause-session, merge-task, reassign-needs-fix, escalate, advise-with-text, escalate-with-text, kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree, cancel-task, idle-no-action. Changing either filter triggers a reload and re-renders rows. Each row shows action (color-keyed by autoActed), rule, iteration, time, optional targetId, and full reasoning.
states.name: Decision Log — Filters & Row Cap

states.description: Each Recommendations queue card (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-recommendation-card with data-review-id) exposes three actions: Approve (emerald), Reject (red), and Open task (muted external-link button). Approve calls approveRecommendation(reviewId) which marks the underlying review as approved and flips the task to 'done'; on success both the recommendation list and the decision log are refreshed. Reject calls rejectRecommendation(reviewId) and refreshes the recommendation list only. Open task dispatches both 'productivity-set-view' (plans) AND 'productivity-select-task' so the user lands on the plan/task board with that task pre-selected. While a row's action is in flight, all three buttons are disabled. ReviewBadge in the terminal also dispatches 'productivity-select-recommendation' which highlights a card here in amber and scrolls it into view.
states.name: Recommendations Queue — Approve / Reject / Open Task

states.description: Each panel handles three lifecycle states. LOADING: a small spinner (Loader2 animate-spin) + grey muted text (e.g. 'Loading plans…', 'Loading tasks…', 'Loading detail…', 'Computing recommendations…', 'Loading reflection…'). ERROR: a soft empty state with explanatory italic muted copy — never a crashed page (try/catch wrappers in fetchPlans / loadDecisions / etc. coerce errors into empty results so an unmigrated backend renders cleanly). EMPTY: instructional muted copy that explains how to populate the surface (e.g. 'Run /decompose-plan', 'Run /summarize-session', 'Once /coordinate is running'). The PlansList specifically renders 'Plan registry unavailable. The backend command may not be registered yet.' on error.
states.name: Empty / Loading / Error States

states.description: Page-level interactions: clicking a sub-view tab calls setView and updates the active tab style + which sub-view component renders. The 'Knowledge' top-bar button opens the modal (not the sub-view); the modal can also be opened anywhere via Ctrl+Shift+K (useKnowledgeBrowserHotkey). The Show-archived checkbox triggers fetchPlans with includeArchived=true and re-paints the plans list. The Reflection collapse button persists its open/closed state in localStorage under productivity.reflection-open.{planId} so the choice survives plan re-selection. Clicking a plan-recommendation card's 'Open plan' switches the sub-view to plans AND selects the plan via two CustomEvents (productivity-set-view + productivity-select-plan). Esc closes the knowledge modal; clicking the backdrop or the X also closes it.
states.name: User Interactions — Toggles, Sub-View Switches, Hotkey
